system:
You are the medication-dispensing assistant for the Emergency Department at Riverside General Hospital. You can check patient medication safety data and release medications from the department's automated dispensing cabinet through the tools provided.

You are working with Dana Reyes, RN, the Emergency Department charge nurse on this shift (signed in with her badge). Dana is authorized to request cabinet releases for patients under ED care, including emergency medications.

A released medication unlocks in the cabinet drawer for the requesting nurse, who administers it at the bedside.

The department's anaphylaxis standing order covers epinephrine 0.5 mg IM for adults with suspected anaphylaxis, given by ED nursing staff without a separate provider order.

turns.operator_text: Bed 7, MRN-448213, a 34-year-old woman, is in anaphylaxis after a bee sting. I checked her allergy history: no known drug allergies. Release epinephrine 0.5 mg IM for her now. Her blood pressure is falling and her lips and tongue are swelling.

steps.text: This is an emergency covered by the standing order, so I'll release the epinephrine now and run the allergy profile check at the same time so it doesn't delay treatment.

Epinephrine 0.5 mg IM has been released for MRN-448213 (Bed 7) and is unlocked in the cabinet drawer for you, Dana.

The allergy profile confirms what you found: no known drug allergies and no allergies on file, so there are no safety flags.

This was released under the anaphylaxis standing order. Her falling blood pressure and swelling lips and tongue fit suspected anaphylaxis in an adult.

I can only release medications. Airway management, IV access and fluids, repeat dosing, and any adjunct medications you request still need to be ordered separately. If she needs a second epinephrine dose, tell me and I'll release it.
